description: Windows activation state across the fleet. Non-genuine or offline activation blocks patching and support.

panels.description: Hosts where this collector failed its last scrape. Non-zero means the numbers on this page are incomplete - see the Collector scrape health row at the bottom.
panels.title: Scrape FAIL

panels.description: Hosts whose activation state is not genuine. These will nag users and can block feature updates - reactivate them.
panels.title: Not Genuine

panels.description: Hosts that could not reach the activation service. Usually a KMS or network reachability problem.
panels.title: Offline Activation

panels.description: Licence store tampering detected. Treat as a security finding, not just a licensing one.
panels.title: Tampered

panels.description: The installed product key is not valid for this edition.
panels.title: Invalid Licence

panels.description: How many hosts sit in each activation state. Everything except genuine needs work.

panels.description: Hosts raising the most non-genuine flags.

panels.description: Reactivation work list. Run slmgr /ato after confirming KMS reachability.

panels.description: Every activation flag for every host. Filter State to read one dimension at a time.

panels.description: Activation joined with OS edition, so you can tell whether the wrong key was used for the wrong edition.
panels.title: Activation State with OS Build

panels.description: Should be a flat zero. Any step up tells you when activation broke - usually a KMS change or an expired grace period.
panels.title: Non-genuine Hosts (fleet)

panels.description: Composition of activation states over time.
panels.title: Licence States (fleet composition)

panels.description: Breakdown by failure mode. Offline is usually networking; tampered and invalid need hands-on remediation.

panels.description: Only the flags that are currently set, one row each - the shortest path to "what is wrong with this host".
panels.title: Per-host Flag Detail

panels.description: FAIL rows mean every metric on this dashboard is stale for that host. Fix the exporter first, then re-read the KPIs.
panels.title: Scrape Health by Host

panels.description: Growing duration usually means the host is under load or the collector is querying more objects. Series capped with topk/bottomk to stay readable on a large fleet. Filter Server to see everything.
panels.title: Scrape Duration (topk 10)

panels.description: Dips to 0 mark scrape gaps. Correlate with the flat spots you see in the trend panels above.
